Meta da aula. Ao final das quatro sessõe: Lesson goal. By the end of the four sessions, you ask yes/no questions and questions with wer, was, wo, woher, wohin, wann and wie, and answer in full sentences.
Camila está na sala de aula. A professor: Camila is in the classroom. The teacher is taking attendance. Jonas sits next to her.
— From Brazil. Now I live in Munich.
— Oi, eu sou o Jonas. Onde você mora?: — Hi, I'm Jonas. Where do you live?
— Legal! Eu também. Vamos tomar um café: — Cool! Me too. Shall we grab a coffee later?
PASSO 1: Há uma segunda armadilha. O por: STEP 1: there's a second trap. Modern English uses "where" for three ideas. German keeps them apart: STEP 2: wo for staying put, wohin for movement towards, woher for movement from — the old English "where, whither, whence".
Em português, uma pergunta de sim ou não: English builds questions with "do": "Do you live in Munich?" German has no "do" at all: the verb itself moves to first position — Wohnst du in München? Think of English "Are you…?" or "Can you…?", where the verb already comes first, and do the same with every verb.

ei = «ai», ie = «i» longo, sch = «x», ch: ei = "eye", ie = long "ee", sch = "sh", ch = soft "kh" (ich) or throaty (Bach), w = "v", v = "f", z = "ts", s + vowel = "z".
O verbo conjugado fica na 2ª posição; a: The conjugated verb goes in 2nd position; a yes/no question starts with the verb — never with "do".
du (um amigo), ihr (vários amigos), Sie: du (one friend), ihr (several friends), Sie (formal, one or several).
der, die, das; todo substantivo com maiú: der, die, das; every noun capitalized; learn the article with the word.
Cinco tipos: -e, -(e)n, -er, sem termina: Five patterns: -e, -(e)n, -er, no ending, -s (often with an umlaut).
ein Tisch, eine Lampe, kein Buch; no plu: ein Tisch, eine Lampe, kein Buch; in the plural, keine.
mein, meine...: concordam com a coisa po: mein, meine…: they agree with the thing owned.
Só o masculino muda: der → den, ein → ei: Only the masculine changes: der → den, ein → einen, kein → keinen.
ich möchte … + segundo verbo no infiniti: ich möchte … + second verb in the infinitive, at the end.

Estes dez erros aparecem com mais frequê: These ten mistakes show up most often in English speakers. Fixing just these makes your German sound far more natural. Read each pair out loud: first the wrong one (to recognize how odd it sounds), then the right one.
Learn the article with the word.
Maiúscula no começo da frase e em todo s: Capital letter at the start of the sentence and on every noun.
The second verb goes to the end.
Como se diz … em alemão?: How do you say … in German?
Wo pergunta pelo lugar onde alguém mora:: Wo asks where someone lives: Wo wohnst du? Wohin asks about a destination and woher about origin.
Pergunte pelo destino: ___ gehst du heut: Ask about the destination: ___ gehst du heute?
O enunciado pede o destino. Wohin signif: We need the destination. Wohin means "where to": Wohin gehst du heute? (Where are you going today?)
Pergunte pela origem: ___ kommt Tom?: Ask about the origin: ___ kommt Tom?
O enunciado pede a origem. Woher signifi: We need the origin. Woher means "where from": Woher kommt Tom? Wohin would ask about a destination.
O enunciado informa que a resposta é uma: The answer is a person, so use wer ("who"): Wer ist das?
Para perguntar pela atividade, usa-se wa: To ask about an activity, use was ("what"): Was machst du heute? Wer asks about a person, not an action.
Qual das três é pergunta de sim ou não?: Which of the three is a yes/no question?
Wohnst du hier? é uma pergunta de sim/nã: Wohnst du hier? is a yes/no question: the conjugated verb comes before the subject. The other options start with question words and ask for specific information.
Complete as perguntas conjugando o verbo: Complete the questions by conjugating the verb: ___ du Deutsch? (lernen) · Wo wohnt Camila? (wohnen)
Com du, lernen passa a lernst. Na pergun: With du, lernen becomes lernst. In a yes/no question, the conjugated verb opens the sentence: Lernst du Deutsch?
Complete as perguntas conjugando o verbo: Complete the questions by conjugating the verb: Lernst du Deutsch? (lernen) · Wo ___ Camila? (wohnen)
Camila corresponde à terceira pessoa do: Camila is third person singular; wohnen becomes wohnt. In a question with Wo, the verb comes right after the question word: Wo wohnt Camila?
Complete as perguntas conjugando o verbo: Complete the questions by conjugating the verb: Woher ___ ihr? (kommen) · Wohnen Sie in München? (wohnen)
Com ihr, kommen passa a kommt. Depois de: With ihr, kommen becomes kommt. After Woher, it's verb then subject: Woher kommt ihr?
Complete as perguntas conjugando o verbo: Complete the questions by conjugating the verb: Woher kommt ihr? (kommen) · ___ Sie in München? (wohnen)
No tratamento formal Sie, wohnen tem a f: With formal Sie, wohnen stays wohnen. A yes/no question starts with the verb: Wohnen Sie in München?
Transforme em pergunta de sim/não na ord: Turn it into a yes/no question, in the order verb–subject–time: Tom arbeitet heute. → ___
Para a pergunta de sim/não na ordem soli: Put the conjugated verb before the subject and keep heute at the end: Arbeitet Tom heute? — no "does" needed.
Relacione a pergunta com a resposta adeq: Match each question to the right answer: (1) Wer ist das? · (2) Was machst du? · (3) Wie alt bist du? · (4) Woher kommst du? · (5) Wo wohnst du? Answers: (a) In Schwabing. · (b) Ich bin 28 Jahre alt. · (c) Das ist Jonas. · (d) Aus Brasilien. · (e) Ich lerne Deutsch.

PASSO 1: O erro que mais custa caro é us: STEP 1: the costliest mistakes: using wo for everything, because English "where" covers all three (a destination needs wohin, an origin woher); keeping the subject before the verb in a question (Wo du wohnst? instead of Wo wohnst du?); looking for a "do" that German doesn't have; and mixing up wer ("who") with "where". STEP 2: read the table and say each correct sentence out loud before you look at the reason.
